reasoning: The underlying PROBLEM — budget-efficient AI control monitoring that decides how much monitor compute a flagged action warrants — is heavily worked on. "Combining Cost-Constrained Runtime Monitors for AI Safety" (Hua et al., NeurIPS 2025) already frames monitoring as a likelihood-ratio (Neyman-Pearson) decision under an average-case budget, deciding when/which monitors to call and more than doubling recall at fixed budget; Ctrl-Z and Ensemble Monitoring study repeated/diverse monitor sampling and resampling. The METHOD (Wald's SPRT) is textbook and has even been applied to LLM evaluation ("Asymptotically Optimal Sequential Testing with Heterogeneous LLMs", arXiv 2604.01086, which uses sequential log-likelihood-ratio testing across LLMs). However, the SPECIFIC angle proposed — using a per-action sequential stopping rule (SPRT) to decide the variable number of repeated queries to the SAME monitor on a flagged action, benchmarked against fixed-N auditing at matched false-alarm/miss rates by replaying control-protocol logs — does not appear directly published; existing AI-control work uses likelihood ratios for monitor selection/intervention thresholds or fixed-count resampling rather than an explicit Wald sequential stopping boundary on repeated draws. So the problem is largely covered but this particular method-combination is an unexplored gap.

evidence.title: Combining Cost-Constrained Runtime Monitors for AI Safety
evidence.summary: Frames AI-control monitoring as a likelihood-ratio (Neyman-Pearson) decision under an average-case cost budget, deciding when and which monitors to call and how to allocate safety interventions; more than doubles recall vs naive baseline in code review. Strongest problem-level match (budget-efficient monitoring via likelihood ratios) but its lever is monitor selection/stochastic calling, not a sequential per-action stopping rule over repeated draws of one monitor.

evidence.title: Asymptotically Optimal Sequential Testing with Heterogeneous LLMs
evidence.summary: Applies Wald-style sequential (SPRT) testing with cumulative log-likelihood ratios to LLM observations from heterogeneous sources, aiming for minimal expected sample size at fixed error rates. Closest method-level match (SPRT over LLM queries), but framed as heterogeneous-source sequential testing rather than the audit-budget AI-control monitoring protocol with replayed control logs.

evidence.title: Ctrl-Z: Controlling AI Agents via Resampling
evidence.summary: Control protocol that resamples flagged untrusted-agent actions (up to several resamples) and audits the most suspicious sample; provides the kind of logged control trajectories the proposal would replay. Uses fixed resampling counts and threshold rules, not a sequential SPRT stopping rule on monitor queries.

evidence.title: Ensemble Monitoring for AI Control: Diverse Signals Outweigh More Compute
evidence.summary: Studies repeated vs diverse monitor sampling under compute constraints, finding diverse 3-monitor ensembles match 12-monitor ensembles at one-quarter compute. Addresses monitor-compute efficiency via fixed ensemble design rather than an adaptive sequential per-action stopping criterion.

evidence.title: Sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) overview
evidence.summary: Confirms SPRT is a well-established sequential hypothesis test using cumulative log-likelihood ratios with accept/reject thresholds set from target error rates, achieving fewer samples than fixed-N tests at matched error rates — i.e., the core statistical machinery of the proposal is standard and not itself novel.
